newsitem.title: UK: Brazil gov't stays with 22 mln bag coffee estimate.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gov't stays with 22 mln bag coffee estimate.

text.p: Brazil's ambassador in London, Rubens Barbosa, said Monday his government was staying with its estimate of Brazilian 1997/98 coffee output around 22 million (60 kg) bags.
He was commenting on last week's U.S. Agriculture Department release of a much higher estimate of 28 million bags than had been expected by traders and analysts.
Barbosa said in response to a request for official comment that Brazil judged the USDA estimate to be "too high. We do not know how they came to this conclusion. We think they are mistaken again.
"We keep our number of 22 million. This is the best estimate we have so far."
The June 13 USDA forecast is up from 27.5 million bags seen for 1996/97. It stunned Brazilian traders because it put the crop currently being harvested as larger than last year.
Barbosa said previous USDA estimates had turned out too high. He also emphasised that he spoke on behalf of Brazil, not as the chairman of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC).
